rows.failed_witness: A combined PowerShell topology wrapper failed to parse before any Git command executed.
The first all-ref semantic-audit wrapper crossed its result window while the exact read-only process continued, leaving no attributable payload.
A PowerShell attempt to pipe a JSON value and Python program through the same pipeline failed to parse before Python started.
The first typewriter-domain slate produced eighteen title collisions at or above the 0.72 threshold.
The collision-free typewriter rewrite still duplicated a well-represented inherited practice domain and was rejected before artifact freeze.
The first schema-aware cat-file replay wrote all requests before reading output and returned no receipt while its process pair remained blocked.
A second overbroad all-ref audit outlived its result handle and left one Python and one Git process without attributable output.
A compound branch-collision PowerShell expression failed to parse before any branch query ran.
A combined branch, path, sparse, and registry projection exceeded its output window without an attributable receipt.
The first new-lane postflight embedded merge-base and LASTEXITCODE inside a property expression and failed to parse.
The first activation-candidate Git-blob hash wrapper completed beyond its result window without an attributable payload.
A source-range projection assumed Select-String returned one object and attempted subtraction on an object array.
The first monolithic x1 patch expected pre-rewrite template lines and failed verification without changing a byte.
The first x1 materialization assumed Liora's final proposal ledger used an outcome key and stopped on KeyError before writing the packet.
Mechanical template preparation placed untracked future x2, final, and tool copies in Tamar's working tree before the x1 freeze, although none was staged or executed.
The first multi-section x2 patch expected a different inherited failure block and failed verification without changing a byte.
A bounded x1 source projection assumed a plausible but nonexistent source-evidence-ledger.json path and stopped before reading any payload.
The first x2 module invocation ran before lifecycle receipts existed: twenty-nine tests passed and the thirtieth stopped on the intentionally absent staged-review receipt.
The first Method Flow validation attempt expected a repository-relative runner that is absent from the exact sparse source and stopped before writing a receipt.
The first exact-staging wrapper used an invalid inline PowerShell exit-code expression; the whole script failed parsing before git add executed.
The first combined receipt-generation wrapper piped directly from a PowerShell foreach statement and failed parsing before any generator or staging command ran.

The first post-evidence equality wrapper printed exact four-way equality and a clean 0/0 divergence, then falsely failed by comparing the tab-delimited value with a literal backtick sequence before manifest replay began.
The first per-entry evidence-manifest replay exceeded its output window and returned no attributable payload after all child processes had exited.
The first template-seed rewrite used a case-insensitive PowerShell hash with both Liora and liora keys and failed parsing before any file changed.
A combined closeout patch expected a validator context that no longer matched the mechanically transformed file and failed verification without changing any byte.
The first final validation receipt classified the frozen semantic-neighbor audit's single rejected typewriter-domain token as an unexpected live stale label and remained invalid.
The first final-validation wrapper relied on ErrorActionPreference and continued to display the invalid receipt after Python returned nonzero; it staged nothing.
The first post-builder probe guessed final-staged-privacy-review.json even though the successful builder had written final-staged-privacy.json, so the read-only probe failed.
The first diagnostic attempted to JSON-serialize a projection containing a PowerShell dictionary shape that ConvertTo-Json rejected before producing an attributable payload.
The first staged-review summary requested nonexistent deletion, unstaged, untracked, and issue fields; PowerShell wrapped each null as a one-item array and displayed misleading counts.
The first successful validation-receipt summary guessed aggregate checks, privacy, strict-JSON, and owner-file fields that were not part of the emitted schema and therefore displayed null.
A refreshed validation summary treated the numeric document_word_guard ceiling as a nested object and wrapped its absent oversized member as a misleading one-item null array.
The first staged-privacy summary guessed candidate_count and scanned_paths fields, which were absent from the emitted receipt even though its exact keys and valid state were returned.
